parts.title: Star Performers
parts.subtitle: Most organisations are looking for talent. But what if they've got it wrong, asks Jeffrey Pfeffer
parts.article:
Star Performers
 
Most organisations are looking for talent. But what if they've got it wrong, asks Jeffrey Pfeffer
 
A One widely held assumption about talent is that it is a reasonably fixed characteristic and it is therefore the job of organisations to identify, recruit and retain star performers. This belief affects the way people are managed in the workplace. Most recruitment decisions are influenced by the skills and abilities of an individual rather than their aptitude and attitude. In terms of career development, organisations invest in staff who have been selected to reach higher-level positions, while ignoring front-line employees and people with less perceived potential. This idea, that talent is a fixed, identifiable characteristic – and that those firms with the best people do the best – is both flawed and harmful to people and organisations. There is a lot of evidence on this point, and it is useful to highlight some of the most pertinent arguments.
 
B First, are there stars? There is no question that in every field, from sports to computer programming to music, there are people who are better than the rest. As psychologist Dean Keith Simonton, who has spent his career studying greatness, has said, 'Wherever you look, the same story can be told. Identify the ten per cent who have achieved the most in a certain endeavour. Count the accomplishments they have to their credit. Now tally the accomplishments of the remaining 90 per cent. The first tally will equal or surpass the second.' For instance, in music, 16 individuals have produced about 50 per cent of the Western classical music that is performed and recorded today, while another 235 composers have produced the remaining half. The more interesting questions concern not the existence of stars, but whether these stars can be reliably identified and, even more importantly, whether their talent is a fixed aspect or can be altered.
 
C Identifying the best people is tricky. Quality of performance changes over time and this is true whether we are talking about professors or footballers. If performance naturally varies, any measurement taken at a single point in time, such as when someone is being hired, will have error and imprecision. Therefore, single assessments of talent are likely to contain mistakes in their categorisation of people. Also, judgements about performance and ability depend on the standards used to judge what is good and bad. It should surprise no-one that for Bach to be considered a great musician, standards of music needed to change to embrace the qualities that his compositions possessed. Similarly, artists and art come in and out of fashion, which means that what is genius depends not only on a person's ability, but on the prevailing standards used to evaluate output.
 
D Finally, it is difficult to evaluate people and their abilities with precision. In the domain of work, research shows that the best predictors of job performance tend to be measures of intelligence. But even these measures correlate only loosely with performance, which means that more than 80 per cent of the variation in performance is unexplained by even the best predictors. Even in the sports arena, where one would think natural ability would be readily assessed because sports teams spend lots of resources on identifying talent, mistakes get made. Basketball star Michael Jordan was dropped by his high school basketball coach and a number of top American football quarterbacks were available early in their careers because they were not considered good enough by various teams.
 
E This leads on to the next question: is talent born or made? Should organisations assume that almost anyone can become a star performer, which implies that there ought to be a greater emphasis on motivation and development, or do they just figure out who is good and who isn't? Here the evidence is clear: talent is at least as much 'created' as inherent and, more importantly, the customary way companies think about identifying talent almost certainly works to destroy a lot of untapped potential. Decades of research by K. Anders Ericsson, professor of psychology at Florida State University, show that exceptional performance doesn't happen without around ten years of nearly daily, deliberate practice for about four hours a day, by people who, with the assistance of their coaches, have access to the best techniques. Once achieved, exceptional performance can't be maintained without relentless effort. So performance may be as much a consequence of training as it is of innate ability, which suggests that performance can be altered by how people are managed.
 
F Further research by Stanford psychology professor Carol Dweck shows that the tendency of organisations to see performance results as an opportunity for an 'assessment' of ability, results in lower performance and poor motivation. Dweck identified two sets of goals that people bring to a performance context: 'performance goals, where the purpose is to validate one's ability or avoid demonstrating a lack of ability, and learning goals, where the aim is to acquire new knowledge and skills'. People with performance goals have been shown to be more prone to helpless behaviour and debilitation after a setback, while people with learning goals strive for higher performance. The implications for managing people and talent are clear. Seeing talent as fixed and job performance as a way of classifying people creates a self-fulfilling prophecy in which ability and intelligence do become fixed. By contrast, seeing ability as malleable leads to a different sort of self-fulfilling prophecy, in which individuals and their employers may invest in ways to enhance performance.

questions.question: disagreement with the view that employing talented people enables companies to achieve top performance

analyses.content: “Disagreement with the view” 对应 “is both flawed and harmful”。
(Paragraph A) “...and that those firms with the best people do the best – is both flawed and harmful...”

题目提到反对“雇佣有才华的人能让公司获得最佳表现”这一观点。原文A段末尾指出：“this idea, that talent is a fixed, identifiable characteristic – and that those firms with the best people do the best – is both flawed and harmful（那种认为'拥有最优秀人才的公司表现最好'的观点既有缺陷又有害）”，明确表达了反对/不同意（disagreement）。

questions.question: a description of what individuals have to do on a regular basis to improve their performance

analyses.content: 题目提到描述个人为了提升表现必须定期做的事情。原文E段中部提到K. Anders Ericsson的研究表明，卓越的表现离不开“around ten years of nearly daily, deliberate practice（大约十年的几乎每天的刻意练习）”，这是对定期行为（regular basis）的具体描述。
“What individuals have to do on a regular basis” 对应 “nearly daily, deliberate practice”。
(Paragraph E) “...exceptional performance doesn't happen without around ten years of nearly daily, deliberate practice...”

questions.question: the evidence that exceptional talent exists in all areas of life

analyses.content: 题目提到卓越才华存在于生活各领域的证据。原文B段开头提到：“in every field, from sports to computer programming to music, there are people who are better than the rest（在每个领域，从体育到编程到音乐，都有比其他人更优秀的人）”，并引用Simonton的话作为佐证。
“All areas of life” 对应 “every field, from sports to...”。
(Paragraph B) “There is no question that in every field... there are people who are better than the rest.”

questions.question: how different ways of evaluating achievement at work can cause different reactions in employees

analyses.content: “Different ways of evaluating” 对应 “performance goals vs learning goals”，“Different reactions” 对应 “prone to helpless behaviour vs strive for higher performance”。
题目提到工作中评估成就的不同方式如何引起员工的不同反应。原文F段详细区分了“performance goals（表现目标）”和“learning goals（学习目标）”两种评估框架，并指出前者导致无助行为（helpless behaviour），后者导致追求更高表现（strive for higher performance），即不同的反应。
(Paragraph F) “People with performance goals have been shown to be more prone to helpless behaviour... while people with learning goals strive for higher performance.”

questions.question: the belief that the time when an assessment is carried out affects its accuracy

analyses.content: 题目提到认为评估进行的时间点会影响其准确性的信念。原文C段前半部分指出：“any measurement taken at a single point in time... will have error and imprecision（任何在单一时间点进行的测量……都会有误差和不精确）”，直接对应题干。
“Time when an assessment is carried out” 对应 “taken at a single point in time”，“Affects its accuracy” 对应 “have error and imprecision”。
(Paragraph C) “...any measurement taken at a single point in time... will have error and imprecision.”

questions.question: the extent to which different talented individuals have contributed to their particular area of achievement

analyses.content: 题目提到不同有才华的个人对其特定成就领域的贡献程度。原文B段通过音乐界的例子（16 individuals produced 50%... another 235 produced the remaining half）量化了不同人才的贡献程度（extent of contribution）。
“Extent to which... contributed” 对应具体的百分比数据（50 per cent）。
(Paragraph B) “...16 individuals have produced about 50 per cent of the Western classical music...”

groups.contentHtml:
33
How many Western classical composers are identified as exceptionally talented?
34
Which composer initially received little recognition for his work?
35
Who can help improve the performance of people practising daily?

analyses.content: (Paragraph B) “...16 individuals have produced about 50 per cent of the Western classical music...”
题目问有多少位西方古典作曲家被认定为特别有才华？原文B段提到“16 individuals have produced about 50 per cent（16个人创作了约50%的作品）”，这些就是指代那些“better than the rest”的卓越人才，填 16。
题目问数量（How many），定位B段的数字统计。
题目问哪位作曲家最初对其作品获得的认可很少？原文C段提到对于“Bach（巴赫）”被认为是伟大的音乐家，音乐标准需要改变（implies initially standards didn't fit him/recognition was low），填 Bach。
“Little recognition” 对应原文 “standards... needed to change to embrace the qualities”。意思是当时的标准不认可他，后来改了标准才认可。
(Paragraph C) “...for Bach to be considered a great musician, standards of music needed to change...”
题目问谁可以帮助每天练习的人提高表现？原文E段提到那些每天刻意练习的人是“with the assistance of their coaches（在教练的帮助下）”，填 coaches。
“Who can help” 对应 “with the assistance of”。
(Paragraph E) “...with the assistance of their coaches, have access to the best techniques.”

questions.question: Companies usually hire people on the basis of their character.

analyses.content: 题目说公司通常根据**性格（character）**招聘人。原文A段明确说：“Most recruitment decisions are influenced by the skills and abilities... rather than their aptitude and attitude（大多数招聘决定受技能和能力影响，而不是天赋和态度/性格）”，题目与原文直接矛盾，选 FALSE。
“Skills and abilities” 是实际依据，而非题目说的 “character（对应 attitude）”。
(Paragraph A) “Most recruitment decisions are influenced by the skills and abilities... rather than their aptitude and attitude.”

questions.question: There are some areas of sport that have a greater proportion of talent than others.

analyses.content: 题目说某些体育领域比其他领域拥有更高比例的天赋人才。原文B段只说“in every field... there are people who are better（在每个领域都有更优秀的人）”，并没有比较不同体育领域之间人才比例的高低，选 NOT GIVEN。
原文说了每个领域都有人才，但没做跨领域的比例比较。

questions.question: Measures of intelligence accurately predict performance at work.

analyses.content: 题目说智力测量能**准确预测（accurately predict）**工作表现。原文D段指出智力测量是最好的预测指标，但即使这些测量也“correlate only loosely（仅有松散的相关性）”，且超过80%的变异是“unexplained（无法解释的）”，即并不准确，选 FALSE。
“Accurately” 与 “correlate only loosely / unexplained” 矛盾。
(Paragraph D) “But even these measures correlate only loosely with performance... more than 80 per cent... unexplained...”

questions.question: There are cases in which talented sportspeople have been overlooked.

analyses.content: 题目说有一些**有天赋的运动员被忽视（overlooked）**的案例。原文D段列举了篮球明星迈克尔·乔丹（Michael Jordan）被高中教练放弃，以及顶级橄榄球四分卫早期被认为“not considered good enough（不够好）”，这些都是被忽视的例子，选 TRUE。
“Overlooked” 对应 “dropped / not considered good enough”。
(Paragraph D) “Basketball star Michael Jordan was dropped... and a number of top American football quarterbacks were... not considered good enough...”

questions.question: Newly formed organisations have the most highly motivated staff.

analyses.content: 题目说**新成立的组织（newly formed organisations）**拥有积极性最高的员工。原文F段讨论了Dweck的两种目标对动机的影响，并未提及“新成立的组织”这一特定类型的公司及其员工动机水平，选 NOT GIVEN。
原文讨论的是管理方式对动机的影响，与公司成立时间无关。
